doc.title: Paquito D'Rivera — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Becoming director of the orchestra in 1970
summary: When Romeu left and members drifted away, Paquito took over for a year and refused to back pop singers.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: What years did you perform in this Orchestra Moderna?
Orchestra started in 1967 and I was main director in 1970.
So you were about 19 when the orchestra started?
And what did being the director, what did that mean? What were your responsibilities?

When the orchestra was dying and everybody was abandoning the boat, Armando retire, I believe or something—I don’t remember when Armando Romeu went—I think he retire, he was very old and ready. He went to another place and was no more director. So, I took care of the orchestra, and I started doing Jazz, and refused to accompany more singers. No more singers, no more pop singers; no, I didn’t want to do that, I want to only Jazz music here, or creative music.
